## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on the integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\), the literal all-degree certificate is established: for every \(0\le k\le i+j+1\), the admissible \(P_{x,k-x}\), including the terminal class, and all one- and two-term Pieri rows are classified below, and their lattice equals \((A_+M)_{d+k}\).
## Strategy
Assume the all-degree integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\), with \(d=ij\), \(i,j\ge1\), and \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\). Put
\[
\alpha_k=\max(0,k-i),\qquad \beta_k=\min(j,k)\qquad(0\le k\le i+j),
\]
and, for \(0\le x\le j,\ 0\le y\le i\),
\[
P_{x,y}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)}
\]
(with a zero final part omitted). Define separately
\[
T:=P_{j+1,0}:=s_{(i+1)^{j+1}}.
\]
Thus no undefined notation such as \(P_{j+1,i}\) is used.

The complete degree bases are
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=\alpha_k}^{\beta_k}\mathbb Z C_x,\qquad
C_x:=P_{x,k-x}\quad(0\le k\le i+j),
\]
and
\[
M_{d+i+j+1}=\mathbb ZT.
\]

For \(1\le t\le k\le i+j\), the admissible sources are exactly
\[
u\in[\alpha_{k-t},\beta_{k-t}],
\]
and Pieri gives, in \(M\),
\[
h_tP_{u,k-t-u}
=
\mathbf1_{u\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]}C_u+
\mathbf1_{u+1\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]}C_{u+1}. \tag{*}
\]
Indeed, an allowed horizontal \(t\)-strip can enlarge either no top row, giving \(C_u\), or exactly one top row, giving \(C_{u+1}\); enlarging two top rows repeats column \(i+1\). A displayed term is omitted precisely when its index is outside \([\alpha_k,\beta_k]\). Hence \((*)\) explicitly classifies every row as zero, one-term, or two-term.

For \(t=1\), all rows are nonzero and are:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&h_1\text{-row}\\ \hline
k>i&h_1P_{\alpha_k-1,k-\alpha_k}=C_{\alpha_k}\\
\alpha_k\le u\le\beta_k-1&h_1P_{u,k-1-u}=C_u+C_{u+1}\\
k>j&h_1P_{\beta_k,k-1-\beta_k}=C_{\beta_k}.
\end{array}
\]
Consequently, there are no one-term boundary rows for \(k\le\min(i,j)\), exactly one for
\[
\min(i,j)<k\le\max(i,j),
\]
and both boundary rows for
\[
\max(i,j)<k\le i+j.
\]

At the terminal degree \(k=i+j+1\), the nonzero Pieri rows are precisely
\[
h_tP_{j,i+1-t}=T\qquad(1\le t\le i+1), \tag{**}
\]
and all other \(h_t\)-rows are zero. For \((**)\), the skew shape \(T/P_{j,i+1-t}\) is the terminal horizontal strip in the bottom row. If \(u<j\), reaching \(T\) requires both a missing top-row box in column \(i+1\) and a bottom-row box in that same column, so the skew shape is not horizontal.

Since \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\),
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=\sum_{t=1}^{k}h_tM_{d+k-t}. \tag{***}
\]
Thus \((*)\) and \((**)\) give every relation.

Writing \(L_k=(A_+M)_{d+k}\), the complete lattice is
\[
L_0=0,
\]
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1})
\qquad(1\le k\le b:=\min(i,j)),
\]
and
\[
L_k=M_{d+k}\qquad(b<k\le i+j+1).
\]
For \(1\le k\le b\), deleting \(C_0\) from the \(k\) adjacent-row matrix gives a lower unitriangular matrix, of determinant \(1\).

For \(b<k\le i+j\), if \(k>i\), use the left singleton \(C_{\alpha_k}\) and the adjacent rows \(C_u+C_{u+1}\) for \(\alpha_k\le u<\beta_k\); their coefficient matrix is lower unitriangular, determinant \(1\). If \(k\le i\), then necessarily \(k>j\), and the right singleton \(C_{\beta_k}\) with those adjacent rows gives an upper unitriangular matrix, determinant \(1\). At \(k=i+j+1\), \((**)\) supplies the \(1\times1\) unit matrix \((1)\). Therefore the displayed lattices equal the full relation lattices in every stated degree.

Hence the requested all-degree certificate is established **conditional on the stipulated all-degree interval/Schur/Pieri presentation**.

## Gaps
The all-degree integral interval presentation, its Schur-basis assertion, and its compatibility with Pieri multiplication are assumed here; they are not independently source-grounded in this certificate. No parent theorem is claimed.

## Next
